Three same-quarter demand reads lean positive on a 3-analyst, $0.7m-a-day name (Audioboom record Q3 on US midterm political ad spend, Spotify ad revenue +10% with podcast sponsorship named, plus 4-5 points of FX and Backyard Ventures on top of organic) against a hard comp that the -13% 60-day drawdown has largely discounted; the bar is one snippet estimate, so every size is capped.

Everything here is public: the 14 Oct pre-close lowered the Q3 bar and the stock already paid 6.5% for it, so on 23 analysts the only unanchored line is 9M cash before customer financing, which is the line that sold the H1 beat (-2.81% on a EUR 1.2bn outflow) and leaves this a near-coin-flip.

On a name with no visible sell-side, the implied H2 EBITDA run-rate from the company's own guide plus H1 makes an upper-half narrowing likelier than a cut, and Rexel's Q3 (Europe same-day +4.5% accelerating, Sweden +4.8%, cable price increases, guide raised again) corroborates the demand half; held back by a +16% 60-day run-up, the first consolidated gearing print and the -7% precedent on the last Q3 narrowing.

A fixed exchange ratio with 0.94 correlation and a 0.35% median daily residual to Vår Energi leaves BlueNord's own Q3 numbers no route to the price; the only live item is whether the release firms up the Danish approvals and closes part of a spread that widened from ~1% to ~2.4% in October, which is small and two-sided.

Two analysts, no published NAV, and the arithmetic sits in the hunter's favour: LFG +26.8% in Q3 prints a record NAV while the discount has widened to 22-23%, which is exactly the condition the company itself said favours buybacks over new investments - and the 2Q26 release moved +9.76% on capital-allocation news rather than on the mechanical NAV.

The toddler BLA guide of 'second half of 2026' was carried in March and April, quietly dropped from the July release and made 'contingent on study completion' on the call, while ClinicalTrials.gov registers COMFORT Toddlers' primary completion for 2026-11 - a guidance line almost certainly moving, on a name that fell the session after 8 of its last 9 releases (median -4.7%) and whose last two BLA-timing resets cost 7.5% and 7.3%; size held back because the 28 Oct date is not issuer-confirmed.

The one argument with content is that Endesa's own APM definition excludes the EUR 208m restructuring provision from the guided metric, so the single visible preview's claim that the provision caps the guide is wrong and 9M ordinary net at ~86% of the guide floor makes 'well above EUR 2.4bn' plausible; but this is a 23-analyst utility at an all-time high above every broker target, so both the move and the edge are small.

The guide line decides this name (new guide +6.91%, plain reiteration -5.42%, upper-half specification +3.47%) and H1 ran at the top of the 3-5% turnover range with core EPS at +9% against a 7-9% guide, so a narrowing tilts up; the weak Q3 phasing is the company's own published aide-memoire and consensus has already been cut ~6%, so nothing here is unpriced and the number stays modest.

The entire Q3 and 9M P&L and balance sheet plus a raised FY guide were pre-released on 12 October, so the scheduled release carries nothing new; a 0.22pp uptick in a 0.83% short register and a weekly-filed buyback are not findings, and this is a correct non-result.

The July guide was explicitly conditioned on fuel not rising significantly from that level and Statistics Finland has diesel going 2.1 to 2.3 to 2.4 EUR/l (+49% y/y), with the covering analyst already at the low end of 33-38m and calling cut risk 'clearly elevated' - but the stock has already fallen ~13% on exactly that story and the company's own habit of warning separately (as it did two weeks after Q2) argues management does not see sub-33m, so the two findings largely offset.

The guidance event already happened on 20 October, so the print is emptied of its driver and what is left is positioning: an all-time high at +17.5% in 20 sessions and +9% in 5, nine to forty points above every target on the company's own consensus page, a Reduce from the covering analyst, and three for three of this name's prior stretched prints falling 10.6%, 9.9% and 5.3%.

Peab's own published list of Q3 orders above SEK 100m is the weakest since at least 2023 (1,649m against 3,881m a year ago) on the line that decided both 2026 prints, and cash flow laps a record +2,792m - but the hunter's own counterexample is decisive for the size: in Q1 2026 the list's direction gave the wrong sign for the reported total and the unlisted residual is 60-80% of Q3 orders.

The guide arithmetic argues for an upward narrowing, but this name sells them (Q2 2026 raised the low end and fell 4.75%), while the reported NOK headline laps a 14-tower Q3 2025 with North American cc growth already decelerating 26% to 12%, tower installs 14 to 11 to 6 and a 6-7% FX headwind, plus an unquantified provision risk on the USD 4.4m Asieris receivable worth ~3% of market cap.

Two unpublished pieces of arithmetic point the same way into a release that is the scheduled slot for a first 2027 harvest guide: the ~6,000t 2026 guide needs 1,694t in Q4 (41% above Q4 2025) and the 8 Oct update pointedly did not restate it, while the first 2026 guide had to be cut 14% and Phase 2 only reaches run-rate mid-2027, against a sell-side marker of ~11,200t; Q3 cost per kg above the pre-released ~65 NOK/kg price adds a negative farming EBITDA.

Consensus FY adj. EBIT of 223 sits at 99% of the top of the 205-225 guide, so the routine Q3 action - raising the low end, as in 2025 - produces a midpoint below the bar and only a top-end raise beats; the stock has run ~21% in three months on no company news into an event that can structurally at best confirm, and the 2025 version of exactly this narrowing drew -1.65%.

A fifth of group EBITDA is already out in Grameenphone's numbers and the rest is peer reads that lean mildly negative on the two units that caused the last two misses - Elisa reporting intensified Finnish competition after the 14 Oct consensus file was struck, and Telia claiming strengthened Norwegian mobile intake - with no company-level datum and a 20-analyst, company-compiled bar, so the size is small either way.

The compiled bar of EUR 209m comparable EBIT is called too high by the covering analyst (182m) and the counterparty evidence agrees - SCA says European NBSK fell slightly in Q3 and Holmen missed - which cuts directly against UPM's own H2 assumption of moderately higher prices; sized down because the same analyst made the same call before Q4 2025 and UPM beat by a third, and because two thirds of EBIT sits outside the softwood read.

Orders are the line that moves this stock (-8.5%, +11.9%, +22.1% on the last three) and two complete board lines were explicitly booked into Q3 with Severn consolidating from 1 July against a weak EUR 1,083m base, while consensus assumes only a flat 12.3% margin despite 2,400 Finns on temporary layoff and Q2's SG&A beat - and the stock drifted -5.75% over 20 sessions into it, which is not a market positioned for an order beat.
